match_note: The peer review file covers only the Nature Communications rounds; it states the manuscript was previously reviewed at another journal, and R2 and R3 both open by referring to a previous round and earlier responses (R3 cites 'our point 3' and an answer about 'Fig. 4d'). The original first-round reports are not in the file, so 'first round' here means NC Version 0, which is already a revision. That version differs from arXiv v1: the title changed (v1: 'Heavy fermions, mass renormalization and local moments in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene via planar tunneling spectroscopy'; NC: 'Local Moment Formation, Entropy Plateaus, Combinatorial Degeneracy, and Heavy-Fermion Mass Renormalization in Magic-Angle Graphene'), the entropy plot moved from Fig. 4c/4d in v1 to Fig. 2e, and the quoted text with '(SI Appendix I)' and the 'ccc-like' sentence do not appear in v1 (v1 cites just '(SI)'). The underlying claims (two entropy plateaus near 10 K and 20 K, heavy-fermion mass renormalization, PTS method) are the same as v1. Reviewer #4 is an early-career co-reviewer with no separate comments; only R2 and R3 raise concerns. R2's report says earlier concerns on PTS vs scanning SET, entropy extraction, temperature calibration and effective-mass interpretation were addressed in the earlier round; those reports are not included. The single rebuttal in the file answers R3's Version 0 comments; R2's comments got no rebuttal.

concerns.quote: the updated entropy plot – now Fig. 2e – seems to be unchanged. As such, we still do not really see plateaus.
concerns.summary: The measured entropy curves do not convincingly show the claimed plateaus, and the promised broader-temperature version of the plot was not visibly changed.

concerns.quote: some of the broader claims regarding heavy-fermion physics and its implications may still rely partly on interpretation rather than entirely unambiguous experimental signatures.
concerns.summary: The heavy-fermion interpretation is partly inferred from a model rather than directly established by unambiguous signatures in the data.

concerns.quote: several individual observables (e.g., compressibility cascades, entropy extraction, and mass renormalization) have been reported in earlier works
concerns.summary: Each observable has been reported before; the novelty rests on combining them in one planar tunneling platform, which R2 accepts as sufficient.

concerns.quote: There is a typo on page 10. “(SI Appendix I)” is written twice
concerns.summary: A duplicated SI citation on page 10.

concerns.quote: There is a typo on page 14, “ccc-like”

notes: C1 response: the authors restated that the first (4-fold) plateau is visible in Fig. 2e, argued the zero-hybridization model is not valid at higher temperature and cannot reproduce the second entropy rise, and added an SI figure (Appendix I, Figure R1) extending the model calculation to 2-100 K plus a phonon-onset estimate (Appendix J); the measured data plot itself was not changed. Round 2 (NC Version 1): R3 'OK with the current version', R4 co-review note only; no new concerns.

first_round.quote: the combination of methodological advance and the reported phenomenology is sufficient to justify publication. Overall, I believe the manuscript, in its revised form, meets the standard for publication in Nature Communications.
While we are convinced by many of the answers, there are still a few remaining points we would like to ask the authors to clarify
I co-reviewed this manuscript with one of the reviewers who provided the listed reports.

recommendations.note: The manuscript was reviewed at another journal first. This file covers only the Nature Communications versions, so 'first round' here means Version 0, which was already a revised manuscript. Referee numbering follows the file (#2, #3, #4); there is no Referee #1. R2 recommends publication without asking for changes but never uses the word 'accept'. Under the stated rule ('publish as is or with small changes' = minor revision) this is inferred as minor revision; read literally it is closest to 'accept'. R3 asks for clarification of the entropy-plateau figure and fixes to two typos, so minor revision is inferred. R4 only co-reviewed and does not name which referee they worked with. R4 is most likely R3's co-reviewer, because R3 writes 'we' and R4 appears alongside only R3 in Version 1. R4 is therefore given R3's recommendation, with that uncertainty noted.
